methodological_rigor.justification: The retrospective single-center cohort of 465 non-metastatic UTUC patients uses a reasonable design with clear inclusion/exclusion criteria, dual-reader splenic volume segmentation with reported intra- and inter-observer ICCs (0.943 and 0.951), and standardization of SV to body surface area. However, important gaps remain: ROC-derived cut-offs (79 cm3/m2 and 21%) are optimized on the same dataset without external or split-sample validation, and the SV cut-off has a weak AUC of 0.526 (95% CI 0.466-0.587) that does not exceed chance, undermining its discriminative basis. Confounders such as smoking, chemotherapy, BMI, and comorbidities that could affect SV and immunity are not modeled, and no sensitivity or competing-risks analyses are presented. Cox proportional hazards and Kaplan-Meier methods are appropriate, effect sizes are reported as HRs with CIs per Table references, but there is no correction for multiplicity across three endpoints and no power calculation, leaving the statistical treatment adequate but not rigorous.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is an individual retrospective cohort study, mapping to Oxford LoE 2b. The proposed dual biomarker (standardized SV plus lym%) is non-invasive, uses routinely available preoperative CT and CBC data, and could plausibly refine postoperative risk stratification in UTUC after RNU. However, it is hypothesis-generating rather than practice-changing: no decision curve, no comparison with or integration into existing prognostic models, and no demonstration that management changes based on SV/lym% improve outcomes, so translational impact is plausible but not demonstrated.

reporting_quality.justification: As a prognostic biomarker study, REMARK is the appropriate standard; the manuscript reports study population, inclusion/exclusion, assay (segmentation) procedure, reader reliability, and univariate/multivariate Cox analyses with adjusted covariates, which covers many REMARK items. Gaps include no explicit pre-specified hypothesis/analysis plan, no details on handling of missing data, no sample-size justification, no reporting of follow-up completeness or flow of patients excluded for <24-month follow-up, and no discussion of model calibration or discrimination beyond the weak AUC. No data or code availability statement is provided, and tables referenced (Tables I-V, Figs. 1-4, supplementary figures) are described but source data are not shared.

novelty_literature.justification: The authors explicitly claim this is the first study to evaluate splenic volume as a prognostic biomarker in UTUC and to combine it with peripheral lym%, which represents a meaningful extension of prior work showing prognostic SV associations in HCC, gastric, colorectal, pancreatic, and NSCLC (refs 16-18, 20, 21, 24). The conceptual contribution is a disease-specific translation of an established pan-cancer observation rather than a new mechanism or methodological innovation. Novelty is therefore a reasonable incremental extension into a new tumor type, but does not open a new paradigm.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well structured with a coherent IMRaD flow, clear abstract, logical progression from rationale to mechanistic discussion, and appropriate use of tables and figures (Fig. 1A study diagram, Fig. 1B ROC, Figs. 2-4 survival analyses, Tables I-V). Language is precise, clinical terminology is consistent, and limitations are acknowledged explicitly. Minor issues include dense paragraphs in the discussion mixing preclinical mechanism with clinical interpretation and some repetition across introduction and discussion, but overall communication is effective.

key_strengths: First study to examine standardized splenic volume combined with lymphocyte percentage as a prognostic biomarker in non-metastatic UTUC after RNU, addressing a documented gap
Reasonable sample size (n=465) with long accrual (2008-2020) and multi-endpoint analysis (OS, CSS, MFS) using Kaplan-Meier and multivariate Cox regression
Rigorous imaging methodology with dual-reader manual segmentation, BSA standardization, and excellent intra-/inter-observer ICCs (0.943 and 0.951)
Non-invasive, low-cost biomarker strategy leveraging routinely available preoperative CT and CBC, supporting clinical feasibility
key_concerns: ROC-derived SV cut-off (79 cm3/m2) has AUC 0.526 (95% CI 0.466-0.587) that does not exceed chance, yet is used as a dichotomization threshold without external validation or sensitivity analyses
Single-center retrospective design with cut-offs optimized on the same cohort risks overfitting and limits generalizability, as acknowledged by the authors
No correction for multiplicity across three survival endpoints; no reporting of missing-data handling, follow-up completeness, or competing risks
Important confounders (smoking, BMI, comorbidities, adjuvant therapy) are not explicitly modeled in the multivariate analyses as presented
No data or code availability statement; REMARK checklist items only partially addressed (no pre-specified analysis plan, sample-size justification, or model calibration)
Mechanistic discussion leans on preclinical literature without direct evidence (e.g., MDSC quantification) in this UTUC cohort
chief_reviewer.rationale: The work is a competent, incremental disease-specific extension of an established pan-cancer biomarker concept with adequate but not rigorous methodology, a weak AUC for the key biomarker, and no external validation or data sharing, aligning with Tier 3 (JIF 4-9.9, e.g., Cancers, Frontiers in Oncology) at best, with major revisions required to strengthen validation and confounder adjustment.
